profile.campus: Stream Chicago, IL submarket (Elk Grove Village, ORDB site, separate campus from Chicago I)
profile.address: 1925 Busse Road, Elk Grove Village, IL 60007
profile.reading: Stream Chicago II sits at 1925 Busse Road in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, internally coded ORDB by the operator. Per Stream own site, the project launched in 2020 with Phase 1 commissioned in the third quarter of 2022, delivering 32 megawatts of capacity at full build across 226,000 square feet, and was reported fully leased by 2023 to unnamed select cloud providers and hyperscale tenants. Chicago II sits in the same Elk Grove Village submarket as Stream separate Chicago I facility on Lunt Avenue, though Stream own site treats the two as sequential, separately developed campuses rather than one shared site, distinguished by different street addresses and different commissioning timelines. A third facility, referred to as Chicago III or ORDC, broke ground in September 2025 nearby on Landmeier Road, planned as more than 1.2 million square feet across three buildings with a dedicated ComEd substation and targeted service in 2027, underscoring the submarket continued growth and Stream sustained investment in the Chicago market. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds completed acquisition of a majority stake in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. Elk Grove Village sits in the O Hare International Airport industrial corridor northwest of downtown Chicago, an area that has become one of the Midwest most significant data center clusters given its fiber connectivity, airport proximity, and interstate access, factors consistent with Stream decision to build successive campuses there over several years rather than scattering its Chicago-area presence across the wider metro.
profile.research_note: 32 MW at full build / 226,000 sqft, launched 2020, Phase 1 commissioned Q3 2022, fully leased by 2023 sourced to Stream own Chicago II page. Explicitly noted as a separate campus from Chicago I per Stream own site.
sources_tried: Streams own dedicated Chicago II page, Streams own Apollo acquisition press release, and Apollos own completion press release

reading.body:
Stream Chicago II in Elk Grove Village is a fully leased data center campus operated by Stream Data Centers, a tier-1 operator now majority-owned by Apollo Global Management as of November 2025. The facility's power capacity is not published. Without a published megawatt figure, this campus cannot be ranked within Illinois' known capacity, though Stream operates at least two other Chicago-area facilities that are tracked separately.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, of which only 6 publish power specifications totaling 236 megawatts of known capacity. Stream Chicago II's unpublished capacity means it does not factor into the state's measured footprint, despite the operator's public positioning as a Fortune 100-serving platform with a 4-plus-gigawatt active pipeline across more than 20 delivered campuses.

The absence of a published specification for this fully leased facility is notable for grid planning. A fully leased site at a tier-1 operator typically runs at or near nameplate capacity, yet the binding constraint on Illinois' AI infrastructure visibility remains the unwillingness of most operators to disclose the power load their tenants are drawing. Without that figure from Stream's own disclosure, the actual demand this campus represents to Illinois' grid cannot be read.
